title: Private Link DNS Resolution

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `dns:query` events with `zone_type="private"` into `index=network`. Confirm UC-4.2.41 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `dns:query` traffic without `zone_type="private"`. Confirm UC-4.2.41 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=network` sourcetype=`dns:query` collected via Custom (DNS query logs), `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=network sourcetype="dns:query" zone_type="private"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.41_private_link_dns_resolut_41"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.41 — Private Link DNS Resolution: queries Microsoft Azure `dns:query` for search criteria `zone_type="private"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Private Link DNS Resolution' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.41 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Forward DNS resolver logs from VNet-linked zones or Azure Firewall DNS proxy. Alert on high NXDOMAIN for PE FQDNs. Validate zone links and auto-registration on new NICs.
visualization: Table (fqdn, fail %), Timeline (DNS errors), Map (source subnet).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=network`.
• Install and configure Custom (DNS query logs), `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `dns:query`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward DNS resolver logs from VNet-linked zones or Azure Firewall DNS proxy. Alert on high NXDOMAIN for PE FQDNs. Validate zone links and auto-registration on new NICs.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=network sourcetype="dns:query" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=network sourcetype="dns:query" zone_type="private"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.41_private_link_dns_resolut_41"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `dns:query` in `index=network` to detect private link dns resolution. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_41_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (fqdn, fail %), Timeline (DNS errors), Map (source subnet)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom (DNS query logs), `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of private link dns resolution so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
